title: God's Army Census
paragraphs: God spoke to Moses in the Sinai Wilderness. It was at the Tent of Meeting, on the first day of the second month, two years after the Israelites left Egypt. God said, “I need a headcount of the entire Israelite community. Go clan by clan, family by family, and get the name of every single male. You and Aaron need to register every man who is twenty years and older and can fight in the army. To make this happen, you'll need some help. Pick one leader from each tribe, the head of his family, to assist you. Here's the squad that will be helping you out:

from Reuben: Elizur son of Shedeur. From Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai. From Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab. From Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar. From Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon. From Joseph's sons—from Ephraim, it's Elishama son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur. From Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni. From Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai. From Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran. From Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel. And from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.”
These were the men hand-picked from the community, all leaders of their ancestral tribes and heads of Israel's military units.

So Moses and Aaron gathered these chosen men and gathered the whole community on the first day of the second month. The people all registered by their tribes and families, listing all the men who were twenty years and older, exactly like God told Moses to do. He counted them all right there in the Sinai Wilderness.
The breakdown for Reuben, Israel's firstborn son: they counted every single guy 20 and up who could go to war, registered by their tribes and families. The tribe of Reuben had 46,500 men.
The count for Simeon's line: every guy 20 and older ready for battle was counted, registered by their clans and families. The tribe of Simeon clocked in at 59,300.
The total for Gad's descendants: they counted every male 20 and up who could fight, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Gad had 45,650 men.
For the tribe of Judah: every guy 20 and older who could fight was counted, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Judah was huge, with 74,600 men.
Next up, Issachar's line: they counted every male 20 and up ready for war, registered by their clans and families. The tribe of Issachar had 54,400.
For Zebulun's tribe: they counted every guy 20 and older who could fight, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Zebulun came in at 57,400.
Now for Joseph's line. From his son Ephraim, they counted every male 20 and up who could fight, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Ephraim had 40,500 men.
And from his other son, Manasseh, they counted every guy 20 and older ready for battle, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Manasseh numbered 32,200.
For the tribe of Benjamin: every guy 20 and older who could fight was counted, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Benjamin had 35,400 men.
Next, Dan's line: they counted every male 20 and up who could go to war, registered by their clans and families. The tribe of Dan was stacked, with 62,700 men.
For Asher's tribe: they counted every guy 20 and older ready for a fight, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Asher had 41,500 men.
And finally, Naphtali's line: they counted every male 20 and up who could fight, registered by their clans and families. The tribe of Naphtali numbered 53,400.

So these are the numbers Moses and Aaron got, with the help of the twelve leaders of Israel, each one representing his family's tribe. The grand total of the Israelite men, 20 years and older, who were able to fight in the army, counted by their ancestral families, was 603,550.

The Levites, though, were a different story. They weren't counted with the others. God had told Moses, “The tribe of Levi is an exception. Don't register them or include them in the main count of the Israelites. Instead, put the Levites in charge of the Dwelling of the Testimony—all its furniture and everything that goes with it. Their job is to carry the Dwelling and all its stuff, take care of it, and camp around it. When it's time to move the Dwelling, the Levites will take it down, and when it's time to set it up, they'll do that too. And for real, anyone else who even gets near it will be executed.

“The rest of the Israelites will set up their tents by their companies, every man in his own camp with his own flag. But the Levites will camp around the Dwelling of the Testimony to make sure God's anger doesn't come down on the Israelite community. The Levites are basically security for the Dwelling of the Testimony.”
And the People of Israel did everything just as God commanded Moses. They followed every single order.

title: Israel's Camp Layout
paragraphs: God spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said, “Here’s the deal. The Israelites need to set up their camp in a big circle around the Tent of Meeting, and everyone has to face it. Each group camps under their own special tribe flag.”
On the east side, facing the sunrise, that’s where Judah’s division sets up under their flag. Their leader is Nahshon, son of Amminadab. His division numbers 74,600 troops.
Next to them, the tribe of Issachar camps. They’re led by Nethanel, son of Zuar, and they’ve got 54,400 people.
And then the tribe of Zebulun is right next to them, led by Eliab, son of Helon, with a crew of 57,400.
The total for Judah's whole section, squad by squad, is 186,400. They get to lead the march whenever everyone moves out.
Down on the south side, you’ve got the camp of Reuben under their flag. Their leader is Elizur, son of Shedeur, with 46,500 troops.
Camping next to them is the tribe of Simeon, led by Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai. They’re packing 59,300 people.
And right next to them is the tribe of Gad, led by Eliasaph, son of Deuel, with a squad of 45,650.
The grand total for Reuben’s side, counting all the troops, is 151,450. They’re the second group in the marching line.
Then, in the middle, there is the Tent of Meeting with the Levites' camp. When it's time to move, every tribe marches in the exact same order they camped, each under their own flag.
Over on the west side are the squads from the camp of Ephraim under their flag, led by Elishama, son of Ammihud. His crew has 40,500 troops.
Next to them, the tribe of Manasseh sets up their camp, led by Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur. They’ve got 32,200 people.
And right beside them is the camp of Benjamin, led by Abidan, son of Gideoni, with a squad of 35,400.
The total number of guys for Ephraim's camp, troop by troop, is 108,100. They’re the third group in the marching order.
Up on the north side are the companies from the camp of Dan under their flag, led by Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai. His crew is 62,700 strong.
The tribe of Asher will camp next to them, led by Pagiel, son of Ocran. They have 41,500 troops.
And next to them is the tribe of Naphtali, led by Ahira, son of Enan, with a squad of 53,400.
The total for Dan's camp is a huge 157,600. They’re the last ones to march out, under their flags.

So yeah, that’s all the People of Israel, counted by their family lines. The grand total in all the camps, troop by troop, was 603,550. But, per God's command to Moses, the Levites weren't counted with the rest of Israel, so they're not in that number.
The Israelites did everything exactly how God told Moses to do it.  They camped under their flags and marched out by tribe with their families.

title: God's Special Team: The Levites
paragraphs: So, here's the rundown on Aaron and Moses's family from when God talked to Moses on Mount Sinai.

Aaron’s sons were Nadab (the oldest), Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. They were all set up to be priests, but then Nadab and Abihu made a serious mistake. They made some kind of rogue offering to God in the Sinai Wilderness and died right there. They didn't have any kids, so only Eleazar and Ithamar were left to serve as priests while their dad, Aaron, was still around.

God spoke to Moses: “Bring the tribe of Levi to Aaron. They will assist him. They’ll work for him and the whole community at the main tent, doing the work for The Dwelling. Their job is to manage all the furniture and equipment, running the operations for the Israelites. Just hand the Levites over to Aaron and his sons; they are the designated crew. Make sure Aaron and his sons are the only ones doing priest stuff. Anyone else who tries to do priest work will be put to death.”

Then God said to Moses, “I’ve picked the Levites from all the Israelites to be a stand-in for every firstborn son. So, the Levites? They're mine. All the firstborn are mine. Remember when I took out all the firstborn in Egypt? I set aside every firstborn in Israel for myself, both people and animals. They belong to me. I’m God.”

God spoke to Moses again in the Sinai Wilderness: “I need you to count the Levites. Go through their families and clans and count every male a month old or older.” So Moses did exactly what God told him to do.
These are the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And here are the clans from Gershon: Libni and Shimei.
Kohath’s clans were from his sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Merari’s clans were from his sons: Mahli and Mushi.
Those are the clans of Levi, family by family.

Gershon was the ancestor of the Libnite and Shimeite clans. All the males a month or older added up to 7,500. The Gershonite clans camped on the west side, right behind The Dwelling. Their leader was Eliasaph, son of Lael. At the main tent, the Gershonites were in charge of The Dwelling itself, its tent, the covers, the curtain at the entrance, the courtyard hangings, the courtyard entrance screen, and all the ropes—basically, everything connected to that stuff.

Kohath was the ancestor of the Amramite, Izharite, Hebronite, and Uzzielite clans. All the males a month or older in these Kohathite clans numbered 8,600. They were in charge of the Sanctuary. The Kohathite clans camped on the south side of The Dwelling, and their leader was Elizaphan, son of Uzziel. They were responsible for the Ark, the Table, the Lampstand, the Altars, all the holy items used in worship, and the screen—everything to do with that.
Eleazar, Aaron's son and a priest, was put in charge of all the Levite leaders. He supervised everyone who was responsible for the Sanctuary — he supervised them all.

Merari was the ancestor of the Mahlite and Mushite clans. The males a month or older in these Merarite clans numbered 6,200. Their leader was Zuriel, son of Abihail, and they camped on the north side of The Dwelling. The Merarites were in charge of the frames of The Dwelling, its crossbars, posts, bases, and all its equipment—all the structural elements. Plus the posts for the courtyard, their bases, pegs, and ropes.

Moses, Aaron, and his sons camped on the east side of The Dwelling, facing the sunrise, right in front of the main tent. They were in charge of the Sanctuary for the Israelites and all the worship rituals. Anyone else who tried to do their job would be put to death.
The grand total of Levites that Moses and Aaron counted, just like God said, clan by clan, all the males one month and older, was 22,000.

Then God told Moses, “Now count all the firstborn sons of the Israelites who are a month or older. Get a list of their names. Then you’re going to set apart the Levites for me—remember, I’m God—and they’ll take the place of all the firstborn Israelites. And their livestock will take the place of the Israelites' livestock. I am God.”
So Moses did what God said and counted all the firstborn of the Israelites. The total number of firstborn males a month or older, all listed by name, was 22,273.

God spoke to Moses one more time. He said, “Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of Israel, and the Levites' livestock in place of their livestock. The Levites are mine. I am God. To redeem the 273 extra firstborn who outnumber the Levites, collect five shekels for each one, using the Sanctuary shekel (twenty gerahs to the shekel). Give that money to Aaron and his sons to redeem those extra Israelites.”

So Moses collected the redemption money from the families of the extra firstborns. For the 273, he collected 1,365 shekels. Then Moses gave the money to Aaron and his sons, exactly as God had commanded him.

title: God's Holy Moving Crew
paragraphs: God spoke to Moses and Aaron: “Count the Kohathite guys from the Levites, men between thirty and fifty who are old enough to work in the Tent of Meeting.
“Here’s the job for the Kohathites in the Tent of Meeting: they’re in charge of the most holy things.

“When the camp is about to move, Aaron and his sons need to go in, take down the curtain, and cover the Ark of the Testimony with it. Then they put a dolphin skin cover on it, a solid blue cloth over that, and slide in the poles.

“Next, they’re to throw a blue cloth over the Table of Presence and put all the plates, incense dishes, bowls, and jugs for drink offerings on it. The special bread that’s always there stays on the table. They cover all that with a scarlet cloth, then a dolphin skin cover, and slide in the poles.
“They’re to use a blue cloth to cover the lampstand and all its gear—the lamps, snuffers, trays, and oil jars. Then they wrap it all up in a dolphin skin cover and put it on a carrying frame.
“They’re to spread a blue cloth over the Gold Altar, cover it with dolphin skins, and put it on a carrying frame.
“They’re to take all the stuff used for serving in the Sanctuary, wrap it in a blue cloth, cover it with dolphin skins, and put it on a carrying frame.

“They need to clean the ashes off the Altar and spread a purple cloth over it. Then they put all the altar tools on it—the firepans, forks, shovels, and bowls, everything—cover it with dolphin skins, and slide in the poles.

“After Aaron and his sons have finished covering up all the holy furniture and items, and the camp is ready to go, the Kohathites will come and carry everything. They must not touch the holy things, or they will die. The Kohathites are the designated movers for everything in the Tent of Meeting.

“Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, is in charge of the lamp oil, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil. He manages the whole Dwelling and everything in it, including all the holy furniture and items.”

God told Moses and Aaron, “Don’t let the Kohathite families be cut off from the Levites. To keep them safe so they live and don’t die when they approach the most holy things, Aaron and his sons have to go in before them and assign each man his specific job and what he has to carry. But the Kohathites themselves can’t even peek at the holy things, not for a second, or they will die.”
God told Moses: “Count the Gershonites by their families and clans. Get all the guys from thirty to fifty years old who are eligible to work in the Tent of Meeting.

“The Gershonites’ job is to carry the heavy stuff: the sanctuary curtains, the Tent of Meeting, its cover, the outer dolphin skin cover, the entrance screens, the ropes, and all the equipment. The Gershonites are responsible for all the work related to these things. All their lifting and moving has to be supervised by Aaron and his sons. You need to tell them exactly what to carry. This is the job of the Gershonite clans at the Tent of Meeting, and Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest, will be their supervisor.
“Now, count the Merarites by their families and clans. Get all the guys from thirty to fifty years old who are eligible to work at the Tent of Meeting.

“This is their specific job at the Tent of Meeting: to carry the frames of the Dwelling, its crossbars, posts, and bases, plus the posts for the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs, ropes, and all their gear. Assign each man exactly what he is supposed to carry. This is the work of the Merarite clans at the Tent of Meeting, supervised by Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.”

So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the community counted the Kohathites by their clans and families. All the men between thirty and fifty who were eligible to work in the Tent of Meeting, counted by their clans, added up to 2,750. This was the total number of Kohathites who served in the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them just like God told them to through Moses.

The Gershonites were counted by their clans and families. All the men between thirty and fifty who were eligible to work in the Tent of Meeting, counted by their clans and families, came to 2,630. This was the total number of Gershonites who served in the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them just as God commanded.

The Merarites were counted by their clans and families. All the men between thirty and fifty who were eligible to work in the Tent of Meeting, counted by their clans, were 3,200. This was the total from the Merarite clans. Moses and Aaron counted them just as God commanded through Moses.

So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel counted all the Levites by their clans and families. All the men between thirty and fifty who came to do the work of serving and carrying the Tent of Meeting numbered 8,580. Following God’s command through Moses, each man was assigned his work and what to carry.
And that’s the story of how they were all counted, just as God commanded Moses.

title: Purity Laws and the Jealousy Test
paragraphs: God spoke to Moses: “Tell the Israelites to send out of the camp anyone who has a serious skin disease, a bodily discharge, or has touched a dead body and become ritually unclean. Whether male or female, send them out. I live among you in the camp; do not defile it.”
The Israelites did just that, kicking them out of the camp. They followed God's orders through Moses, no questions asked.

Then God told Moses, “Tell the Israelites, if a man or woman sins, breaking faith with God. They're guilty. First, they have to own up to their sin. Then, they have to pay back the person they wronged in full, plus an extra 20 percent. If the person they wronged is gone and has no family to receive the payment, then the money goes to God, which means it's given to the priest. They also have to bring a ram to make things right. And from now on, any holy offerings the Israelites bring to a priest, belong to that priest. What's yours is yours, but what you give to the priest is his to keep.”

God then said to Moses, “Okay, tell the Israelites this. If a man’s wife goes astray, sleeping with another man, but he has no clue. She's defiled herself, but there were no witnesses, she wasn't caught red-handed. But then, the husband starts getting this crazy jealous feeling, and he suspects his wife is impure. It doesn't even matter if she's actually innocent and his jealousy is all in his head. Here's what he has to do: he takes his wife to the priest. He also has to bring an offering for her—two quarts of barley flour. No fancy oil or incense on it, because this is a jealousy offering, an offering to bring the truth out into the light.

“The priest will then take her and make her stand before God. He'll grab a clay jar with some holy water and mix in some dust from the floor of the holy tent. After the priest has her stand there in God's presence, he will loosen her hair and put the special offering in her hands—the jealousy offering—while he holds the bitter water that brings a curse. Then the priest puts her under oath, saying, ‘If you haven't slept with anyone else, and you haven't cheated and become impure while married to your husband, then this bitter, curse-bringing water won't hurt you. But if you HAVE cheated while married, and you HAVE defiled yourself by sleeping with another man...’—and here the priest lays down the curse—‘then may God make you a curse word among your people. He will make your womb shrivel up and your belly swell. Let this curse-water enter your body, make your belly swell and your womb shrivel.’
“And the woman has to say, ‘Amen. Amen.’

“The priest then writes these curses on a scroll and washes the ink into the bitter water. He then makes the woman drink the bitter water that brings the curse. This water will go inside her and cause pain. The priest will take the jealousy offering from her hands, wave it before God, and bring it to the altar. He'll then take a handful of the offering, as a symbol, and burn it on the altar. After that, he makes her drink the water. If she was unfaithful and defiled herself, when she drinks the curse-water, it will enter her and cause pain; her belly will swell up and her womb will shrivel. She'll be a cautionary tale among her people. But if she's innocent and hasn't defiled herself, she'll be cleared and will be able to have kids.

“So that's the law for jealousy. It's for when a wife cheats and defiles herself while married, or when a husband feels jealous and suspects his wife. The priest has to make her stand before God and do this whole ritual. The husband will be cleared of any wrongdoing, but the woman will have to pay the price for her sin.”

title: The Nazirite Vow
paragraphs: God spoke to Moses: “Tell the Israelites, if any of you—guy or girl—wants to make a special Nazirite vow, as a dedication to God: You gotta lay off all wine and beer, any kind of alcohol, not even grape juice. You cannot even eat grapes or raisins. For the whole time you're consecrated, nothing from a grapevine is allowed—not the seeds, not even the skin.
Also, for the entire time you're doing this, you can't get a haircut. Your long hair is the sign that you're set apart for God.

And another major rule: while you're consecrated to God, you can't go near a dead body. Even if it's your own dad, mom, brother, or sister who passed away, you can't make yourself spiritually unclean, because the sign of your commitment to God is right there on your head.
For the whole time of your vow, you are holy to God.

Now, if someone dies suddenly beside you, and your consecrated hair gets 'defiled,' you have to shave your head on the seventh day, the day you get purified. Then on the eighth day, bring two doves or two pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the main tent. The priest will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to make you right with God after being near the corpse. You re-dedicate your hair that same day and restart your Nazirite vow by bringing a one-year-old lamb as a special offering. You must start over; the time before doesn't count because your vow got messed up.

When your time of being dedicated to God is over, here are the instructions. First, you go to the entrance of the main tent. Then you give your offerings to God: a healthy one-year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, a healthy one-year-old female lamb for a sin offering, a healthy ram for a peace offering, and a basket of bread made without yeast—loaves made with fine flour mixed with oil, and wafers spread with oil, along with the regular grain and drink offerings. The priest will go to God and offer up your sin offering and burnt offering. He'll sacrifice the ram as a peace offering to God with the basket of bread, and finally, the grain and drink offerings.
At the entrance of the main tent, you'll shave off all that hair you grew out and throw it into the fire that's burning under the peace offering.

After you've shaved, the priest will take a boiled shoulder from the ram, a piece of the bread, and a wafer from the basket and put them in your hands. The priest will then wave them in front of God as a special wave offering. They're holy and belong to the priest, along with the breast and thigh that were also offered.
And now, you're finally free to drink wine again.

So yeah, those are the rules for Nazirites when they bring their offerings to God for their special vow, on top of any other offerings they give. They have to follow through with the vow they made, exactly as these instructions say.
God told Moses: “Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the people of Israel. Say to them:

May God bless you and keep you,
May God smile on you and be gracious to you,
May God look you in the eye and give you peace.
In this way they will put my name on the People of Israel, and I will bless them."

title: The 12-Day Dedication Offerings
paragraphs: When Moses was done setting up the holy tent, he blessed it and made it sacred, along with everything in it. He did the same for the altar and all its gear.

The leaders of Israel, the heads of the family tribes who were in charge of the big count, brought their gifts. They came to God with six covered wagons and twelve oxen—a wagon for every two leaders and an ox from each one.
God told Moses, “Take these to use for moving the Tent of Meeting. Give them to the Levites based on what they need for their jobs.”

Moses took the wagons and oxen and handed them over to the Levites. He gave two wagons and four oxen to the Gershonites for their work, and four wagons and eight oxen to the Merarites for theirs. They were all working under Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest. But Moses didn't give any to the Kohathites because their job was to carry the holy items on their own shoulders.

When the altar was blessed, the leaders brought their offerings to dedicate it. They presented them right in front of the altar because God had told Moses, “One leader each day will bring his offering to dedicate the altar.”
On day one, Nahshon son of Amminadab, from the tribe of Judah, brought his gift. His offering was:

a silver plate weighing three and a quarter pounds and a silver bowl weighing one and three-quarter pounds (according to the standard Sanctuary weights), each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a Grain-Offering;
a gold vessel weighing four ounces, filled with incense;
a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old lamb for a Burnt-Offering;
a male goat for a Sin-Offering;
and for a Peace-Offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old lambs.
That was the offering from Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On day two, Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, brought his gift. His offering was:

That was the offering from Elishama son of Ammihud.
On day eight, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, the leader of the Manasseh people, brought his gift. His offering was:

a silver plate weighing three and a quarter pounds and a silver bowl weighing one and three-quarter pounds (according to the standard Sanctuary weights), each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a Grain-Offering;
a gold vessel weighing four ounces, filled with incense;
a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old lamb for a Burnt-Offering;
a male goat for a Sin-Offering;
and for a Peace-Offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old lambs.
That was the offering from Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
On day nine, Abidan son of Gideoni, the leader of the Benjamin people, brought his gift. His offering was:

a silver plate weighing three and a quarter pounds and a silver bowl weighing one and three-quarter pounds (according to the standard Sanctuary weights), each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a Grain-Offering;
a gold vessel weighing four ounces, filled with incense;
a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old lamb for a Burnt-Offering;
a male goat for a Sin-Offering;
and for a Peace-Offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old lambs.
That was the offering from Abidan son of Gideoni.
On day ten, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, the leader of the Dan people, brought his gift. His offering was:

a silver plate weighing three and a quarter pounds and a silver bowl weighing one and three-quarter pounds (according to the standard Sanctuary weights), each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a Grain-Offering;
a gold vessel weighing four ounces, filled with incense;
a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old lamb for a Burnt-Offering;
a male goat for a Sin-Offering;
and for a Peace-Offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old lambs.
That was the offering from Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
On day eleven, Pagiel son of Ocran, the leader of the Asher people, brought his gift. His offering was:

a silver plate weighing three and a quarter pounds and a silver bowl weighing one and three-quarter pounds (according to the standard Sanctuary weights), each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a Grain-Offering;
a gold vessel weighing four ounces, filled with incense;
a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old lamb for a Burnt-Offering;
a male goat for a Sin-Offering;
and for a Peace-Offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old lambs.
That was the offering from Pagiel son of Ocran.
On day twelve, Ahira son of Enan, the leader of the Naphtali people, brought his gift. His offering was:

a silver plate weighing three and a quarter pounds and a silver bowl weighing one and three-quarter pounds (according to the standard Sanctuary weights), each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a Grain-Offering;
a gold vessel weighing four ounces, filled with incense;
a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old lamb for a Burnt-Offering;
a male goat for a Sin-Offering;
and for a Peace-Offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old lambs.
That was the offering from Ahira son of Enan.
So these were the dedication gifts from the leaders of Israel when the altar was blessed:
twelve silver plates, twelve silver bowls, twelve gold vessels.

Each plate weighed three and a quarter pounds and each bowl one and three-quarter pounds. All together, the plates and bowls together weighed about sixty pounds (by the official Sanctuary weight). The twelve gold vessels filled with incense weighed four ounces each (by the official Sanctuary weight). All together, the gold vessels weighed about three pounds.
The grand total of animals for the Burnt-Offering, plus the Grain-Offering, was:
twelve bulls, twelve rams, twelve one-year-old lambs.
For the Sin-Offering:
twelve male goats.
The grand total of animals for the Peace-Offering sacrifice was:
twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, sixty one-year-old lambs.
These were all the offerings for dedicating the altar after it was blessed.

When Moses went into the Tent of Meeting to talk with God, he heard the Voice talking to him from between the two angel-cherubim on top of the Atonement-Cover on the Ark of the Covenant. He spoke with him.

title: Setting Apart the Levites
paragraphs: God spoke to Moses: “Tell Aaron, ‘Set up the seven lamps so they shine light out in front of the Lampstand.’”

So Aaron did exactly that. He set up the lamps to light up the area in front of the Lampstand, just like God told Moses. The whole Lampstand was made of hammered gold, from the base to the flower designs. It was a perfect copy of the design God had shown Moses.

Then God said to Moses, “Take the Levites out from the rest of the Israelites and purify them. Here’s how you’ll do it: Sprinkle them with water that makes them pure, have them shave their whole bodies, and make them wash their clothes. Then they will be clean.

“Get them to bring a young bull with the grain offering that goes with it—that’s fine flour mixed with oil. And you'll need a second young bull for a sin offering. Bring the Levites to the front of the Tent of Meeting and get the whole community of Israel to gather around. Present the Levites to God, and have the Israelites lay their hands on them. Then Aaron will present the Levites to God as a special offering from the people, so they’re ready to do God’s work.

“Have the Levites put their hands on the bulls' heads. One bull is for the sin offering, and the other is for the burnt offering to God to make things right for the Levites. Then have the Levites stand in front of Aaron and his sons, and present them as a special offering to God. This is how you officially set the Levites apart from everyone else in Israel; the Levites are 100% mine.

“After you’ve made them pure and presented them as a special offering, they can start their jobs at the Tent of Meeting. The Levites have been hand-picked from the Israelites just for me; they’re taking the place of every firstborn son from an Israelite family. Every firstborn in Israel, whether it's a person or an animal, is mine. When I took out all the firstborns in Egypt, I set them apart for my holy use. But now, I’m swapping in the Levites for every firstborn son in Israel. I’ve picked them out and given them to Aaron and his sons to do all the work at the Tent of Meeting for the rest of the Israelites and to make things right for them, so that nothing bad happens to the people when they get close to the Holy Place.”

Moses, Aaron, and the whole community of Israel did all this with the Levites, exactly as God had commanded Moses. The Levites got themselves clean and washed their clothes. Then Aaron presented them as a special offering to God and made things right for them to make them pure. Only after all that did the Levites start their work at the Tent of Meeting. Aaron and his sons were in charge, telling them what to do based on the instructions God had given.

God told Moses: “Here are the rules for the Levites: From twenty-five years old, they start working at the Tent of Meeting. At fifty, they must retire. They may assist their brothers with tasks at the Tent, but they can’t do the main work themselves. These are the official rules for the Levites’ jobs.”
changes: Badges realigned to MSG units; slang cleaned

title: Passover and the Cloud
paragraphs: God spoke to Moses in the Sinai Wilderness. It was the first month of the second year after they left Egypt. 'Tell the Israelites to celebrate Passover at the appointed time. Do it on the evening of the fourteenth day of this month, and follow all the rules.'
Moses passed the message to the Israelites, and they did it. They celebrated Passover in the Sinai Wilderness on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month, just like God told Moses.

But some men could not celebrate because they were 'unclean' from touching a dead body. So they went to Moses and Aaron and said, 'We are unclean because of a corpse, but why should we miss out on giving God our offering with everyone else?'
Moses said, 'Wait here; let me find out what God commands concerning you.'

God told Moses: 'Tell the Israelites: If you're unclean from a corpse, or are on a journey, you can still celebrate Passover. Just do it on the fourteenth day of the *second* month in the evening. Eat the lamb with flatbread and bitter herbs. Don't save any leftovers for the morning, and don't break any of the lamb's bones. Follow all the rules.'

'But if someone is clean and not on a trip and *still* skips Passover, they're cut off from the community. They didn't bring God's offering at the right time, so they have to face the consequences for their sin.'
'And any foreigner living with you who wants to celebrate Passover may do it, but they must follow all the same rules. The rules are the same for everyone, whether you're a foreigner or born here.'

The day the Tabernacle was set up, a cloud covered it. From sunset to sunrise, the cloud over the Tabernacle looked like fire. It was always like that—a cloud by day and what looked like fire by night.

Whenever the cloud lifted from the Tent, the Israelites would pack up and move. And wherever the cloud settled, they'd set up camp. They moved when God said move, and they stayed when God said stay. As long as the cloud was over the Tabernacle, they stayed put. Even if the cloud stayed for a long time, they respected God's command and didn't move. They stayed in camp, following God's orders, as long as the cloud was there. But the second God gave the signal, they were on the move. If the cloud only stayed from evening to morning and then lifted, they marched. Day or night, it didn't matter—when the cloud lifted, they marched. It didn't matter if the cloud stayed for two days, a month, or a whole year. As long as the cloud was there, they were there. And when the cloud went up, they got up and marched. They camped when God said to, and they marched when God said to. They were living on God's schedule, as told to them by Moses.
changes: Badges realigned to MSG units; slang cleaned

title: The March Begins
paragraphs: God spoke to Moses: “Make two trumpets out of hammered silver. Use them to call everyone together and to give the marching orders to the camps. When you blow them both, the whole community will gather at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

“When you blow a single short blast, that’s the signal for the leaders, the heads of the clans, to meet up. When you give a long blast, that’s the signal to march. The first long blast, and the tribes camped on the east side head out. The second long blast, the camps on the south side head out. The long blasts are for marching. The call to get everyone together is a different sound from the marching signal.

“Aaron’s sons, the priests, are the ones who have to blow the trumpets; that’s their job forever. When you go to war against an enemy who’s coming at you, blow a long blast on the trumpet so God will notice you and save you from your enemies. Also, on your celebration days, your appointed feasts, and New Moon festivals, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace offerings. They’ll be a reminder to focus on God. I am God, your God.”

In the second year, on the twentieth day of the second month, the Cloud lifted from over the Dwelling of the Testimony. That was the signal, and the people of Israel started their journey from the Wilderness of Sinai. The Cloud finally stopped and settled in the Wilderness of Paran. They started their march just like God had commanded through Moses.

The divisions of the camp of Judah went first, under the command of Nahshon son of Amminadab. Nethanel son of Zuar was in charge of the tribe of Issachar's forces, and Eliab son of Helon was in charge of the tribe of Zebulun's forces. As soon as the Dwelling was taken down, the Gershonites and Merarites, who carried it, set out.

Next up was the flag for the camp of Reuben, with Elizur son of Shedeur in command. Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was in charge of the tribe of Simeon's forces, and Eliasaph son of Deuel was in charge of the tribe of Gad's forces. Then the Kohathites, who carried the holy items, left. The plan was for the Dwelling to be set up by the time they got to the new spot.

The flag for the tribe of Ephraim moved out next, with Elishama son of Ammihud in command. Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was in charge of the tribe of Manasseh's forces, and Abidan son of Gideoni was in charge of the tribe of Benjamin's forces.

Last of all, under the flag of the tribe of Dan, the rear guard for all the camps marched out, with Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai in command. Pagiel son of Ocran was in charge of the tribe of Asher's forces, and Ahira son of Enan was in charge of the tribe of Naphtali's forces.
These were the marching groups of the people of Israel. They were on their way.

Moses said to his brother-in-law, Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, “We are going to the place God promised, saying, ‘I’ll give it to you.’ You should come with us; we will treat you well. God has promised good things for Israel.”
But Hobab said, “No, I will not go. I am going back to my own land and my own people.”
Moses said, “Please do not leave us. You know all the best spots to camp in the wilderness. You can be our eyes. If you come with us, we will share with you whatever good things God does for us.”

So they finally marched out. They marched for three days from the Mountain of God, with the Chest of the Covenant of God leading the way to find them a place to camp. The Cloud of God was over them during the day as they marched. Whenever the Chest started moving, Moses would say:
“Get up, God! Scatter your enemies! Make your enemies flee!”
And when the Chest was set down, he would say:
“Rest with us, God. Stay with the thousands and thousands of Israel.”
changes: Badges realigned to MSG units; Hobab dialogue restored; slang cleaned

title: Complaints, Manna, and Quail
paragraphs: The people started complaining about their hardships. God heard it and his anger was kindled. His anger flared up, and a fire literally blazed out and started burning the edges of the camp. The people cried out to Moses for help. Moses prayed to God, and the fire died down. They named that place Taberah, which means 'Blaze,' because, well, a fire from God had blazed up against them.

Then, the rabble among them had a strong craving, and pretty soon they had all the Israelites whining, 'Oh, for meat! Remember the fish we used to eat in Egypt—for free! Not to mention the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic. But out here, nothing tastes good. All we ever get is this manna, manna, manna.'

Manna was this seed-like thing that looked kinda shiny, like resin. The people would go around, gather it, and then grind it up or pound it into a powder. They'd boil it and make little cakes out of it. It tasted like a fancy pastry cooked in olive oil. When the dew came down on the camp at night, the manna just showed up with it.
Moses heard all the whining. Every family was just complaining right outside their tents. God's anger was boiling over, and Moses could see things were getting really bad.

Moses said to God, 'Why are you treating me this way? What did I do to you to get stuck with this? Did I give birth to these people? Am I their mom? So why are you making me responsible for them? Why are you telling me to carry them around like a baby, all the way to the land you promised their ancestors? Where am I supposed to get meat for all these people who are whining at me, ‘Give us meat; we want meat.’ I can't handle this by myself—it's way too much. If this is how you're going to treat me, just do me a favor and kill me now. I'm so done. Just let me out of this.'

God said to Moses, 'Gather seventy men from Israel's leaders, guys you know are respected and responsible. Bring them to the Tent of Meeting, and I'll meet you there. I'll come down and talk with you, and I'll take some of the Spirit that's on you and put it on them. They'll be able to help you carry the burden of these people, so you won't have to do it all alone.'

'And tell the people: Get yourselves ready. Tomorrow, you're gonna eat meat. You've been whining to God, ‘We want meat! Life was better in Egypt!’ Well, God heard you, and he's gonna give you meat. You're gonna eat it. And not just for one day, or two, or five, or ten, or twenty. You're gonna eat meat for a whole month. You'll eat so much meat it'll start coming out of your nose. You'll be so sick of it you'll want to puke just thinking about it. And you know why? Because you've rejected God, who's right here with you, and you've whined to his face, ‘Ugh, why did we ever leave Egypt?’’

Moses said, 'I am among 600,000 men, and you're saying you'll give them meat every day for a month? Where's that gonna come from? Even if we butchered every single one of our flocks and herds, would that be enough? Even if we caught every fish in the ocean, would that be enough?'
God said to Moses, 'Is my arm too short? You're about to see whether what I say happens or not.'

So Moses went out and told the people what God said. He got seventy of the leaders together and had them stand around the Tent. God came down in a cloud, spoke to Moses, and took some of the Spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy leaders. When the Spirit rested on them, they started prophesying. But it was a one-time thing; it didn't happen again.

Meanwhile, two guys named Eldad and Medad had stayed behind in the camp. They were on the list of leaders but didn't go to the Tent. But the Spirit came on them too, and they started prophesying right there in the camp.
A young guy ran and told Moses, 'Hey, Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!'
Joshua, the son of Nun, who had been Moses's top assistant since he was young, said, 'Moses, my lord, stop them!'
But Moses said, 'Are you jealous for my sake? I wish all of God's people were prophets. I wish God would put his Spirit on all of them.'

Then Moses and the leaders of Israel went back to the camp. A wind sent by God blew in a ton of quail from the sea. They piled up like three feet deep all over the camp, and for a day's walk in every direction. The people were out gathering quail all day, all night, and all the next day—it was a crazy amount. Even the slowest person gathered at least sixty bushels. They spread them all out around the camp to dry. But while the meat was still in their mouths, before they'd even really swallowed, God's anger exploded against them. He hit them with a terrible plague. They ended up naming that place Kibroth Hattaavah, which means 'Graves of the Craving,' because that's where they buried the people who had been craving meat.
From Kibroth Hattaavah, they moved on to Hazeroth and stayed there for a while.
changes: Badges realigned to MSG units; slang cleaned; 600,000/70/three feet/sixty bushels verified present

title: Miriam Challenges Moses
paragraphs: So, Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because he had married a Cushite woman.
They said, “Has God only spoken through Moses? Hasn’t he also spoken through us?”
God heard this.
Now Moses was very humble, more humble than anyone else on earth.
God said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “Come out to the Tent of Meeting, all three of you.” So the three of them went.
God came down in a massive pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance to the Tent. He called for Aaron and Miriam. When they stepped up, He said:

“Listen to my words: If there’s a prophet of God here, I make myself known to them in visions, I talk to them in dreams. But it’s not like that with my servant Moses. He has the run of my entire house. I speak to him face to face, clearly and not in riddles. He sees the form of God. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses? That was wild.”
The anger of God just blazed out at them. And then He was gone.
When the cloud lifted from the Tent, oh man… Miriam had turned leprous, her skin as white as snow. Aaron took one look at Miriam and saw she was a leper!

He said to Moses, “Please, my lord, do not hold against us the sin we have so foolishly committed. Please don’t let her be like a stillborn baby, coming out of its mother’s womb with half its body rotted away.”
And Moses prayed to God:
“Please, God, heal her. Please, heal her.”
God answered Moses, “If her own father had spit in her face, wouldn’t she be shamed for seven days? So, quarantine her outside the camp for seven days. Then she can come back.”
So Miriam was quarantined outside the camp for seven days. The people didn’t move on until she was brought back in. Only then did the people leave Hazeroth and set up camp in the Wilderness of Paran.
changes: Badges realigned to MSG units; title/slang cleaned

title: Scouting Canaan
paragraphs: God spoke to Moses: "Send some men to scout the land of Canaan, which I'm giving to the Israelites. Pick one leader from each of the main family groups, and make sure they are leaders."
Following God's orders, Moses sent them out from the Desert of Paran. All of them were leaders in Israel, one from each tribe. Their names were:

from Reuben: Shammua son of Zaccur
from Simeon: Shaphat son of Hori
from Judah: Caleb son of Jephunneh
from Issachar: Igal son of Joseph
from Ephraim: Hoshea son of Nun
from Benjamin: Palti son of Raphu
from Zebulun: Gaddiel son of Sodi
from Manasseh (a Joseph tribe): Gaddi son of Susi
from Dan: Ammiel son of Gemalli
from Asher: Sethur son of Michael
from Naphtali: Nahbi son of Vophsi
from Gad: Geuel son of Maki.
from Reuben: Shammua son of Zaccur
from Simeon: Shaphat son of Hori
from Judah: Caleb son of Jephunneh
from Issachar: Igal son of Joseph
from Ephraim: Hoshea son of Nun
from Benjamin: Palti son of Raphu
from Zebulun: Gaddiel son of Sodi
from Manasseh (a Joseph tribe): Gaddi son of Susi
from Dan: Ammiel son of Gemalli
from Asher: Sethur son of Michael
from Naphtali: Nahbi son of Vophsi
from Gad: Geuel son of Maki.
Those are the names of the men Moses sent to scout the land. Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.

When Moses sent them to scout Canaan, he instructed them: "Go up through the Negev and into the hill country. See what the land is like. Examine the people: are they strong or weak? Are they many or few? Is the land good or bad? Look at their towns: are they just open camps or are they like actual fortresses? And the soil—is it good for farming or is it dead? See if there are any forests. Oh, and try to bring back some of their food so we can see what's up. It's grape season, so grab some if you can."

And just like that, they were off. They explored the whole area from the Zin Desert all the way to Rehob, near Lebo Hamath. Their route took them through the Negev to Hebron, where these giants, the descendants of Anak, were living—Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai. Fun fact: Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt. When they got to Eshcol Valley, they found a cluster of grapes so massive it took two guys to carry it on a pole. They also grabbed some pomegranates and figs. They named the place Eshcol Valley (which basically means Grape-Cluster-Valley) because of that wild bunch of grapes. After 40 days on their recon mission, they headed home.
They showed up in front of Moses, Aaron, and all the Israelites at Kadesh in the Paran Desert. They gave their report to everyone and showed off the fruit they brought back. They reported:

"We went to the land you sent us to, and it does flow with milk and honey! Here is its fruit. The only problem is, the people there are fierce, and their cities are huge and super fortified. Even worse, we saw the descendants of the giant Anak there. Amalekites are all over the Negev; Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites are in the hills; and the Canaanites have the coast and the area along the Jordan River."
Caleb silenced the people before Moses and said, "We should go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly do it."

But the men said, "We can't attack those people; they are stronger than we are." They started spreading scary rumors among the Israelites, saying, "We scouted the whole land, and it's a place that just eats people up. Everyone we saw was massive. We even saw the Nephilim there. We seemed like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and we looked the same to them. And that's exactly how they looked at us, like we were nothing."
changes: Badges realigned (scout list=MSG 3-15 split); slang cleaned; Vophsi/Geuel names verified

title: Rebellion and Punishment
paragraphs: The whole community wept and complained all night. All the Israelites were grumbling about Moses and Aaron. The whole crowd was in on it, saying, “We should’ve just died in Egypt! Or even out here in the wilderness! Why did God bring us to this country just to get us killed? Our wives and kids are gonna be captured. Why don’t we just go back to Egypt?”
Pretty soon, they were all saying to each other, “Let’s get a new leader and head back to Egypt.”
Moses and Aaron just fell on their faces in front of everyone, who had gathered for this emergency meeting.

Joshua, son of Nun, and Caleb, son of Jephunneh, who were part of the spy team, tore their clothes in frustration. They told the crowd of Israelites, “The land we scouted is very good. If God is happy with us, He’ll lead us into that land, a place that’s flowing with milk and honey, just like they say. And He’ll give it to us. Just don’t rebel against God! And don’t be scared of those people. We will have them for lunch. They have no protection, and God is with us. Don’t be afraid of them!”
But now the whole community was furious and started talking about stoning them.

The Glory of God appeared at the Tent of Meeting. Every single Israelite saw it. God said to Moses, “How long are these people going to disrespect me? How long will they refuse to trust me, even after all the miracles I’ve done for them? I will strike them with a plague and destroy them. But I’ll make you into a nation that’s bigger and stronger than they ever were.”

But Moses said to God, “The Egyptians are going to hear about this! You brought these people out of Egypt with a huge display of power, and now this? The Egyptians will tell everyone. They already know you are God, that you’re on this people’s side, that you’re right here with them. They see you with their own eyes in your Cloud that hangs over them, and in the Pillar of Cloud that leads them by day and the Pillar of Fire by night. If you kill all these people at once, all the nations who’ve heard about you will say, ‘God couldn’t bring these people into the land He promised them, so He just killed them in the wilderness.’
“So now, please, let your power be shown, make it huge, just like you said before when you told us,

‘God, you are slow to get angry and full of loyal love, forgiving wickedness, rebellion, and sin. But you never just ignore sin. You let the consequences of parents’ sins affect their children, even to the third and fourth generation.’
“Please forgive the messed-up actions of this people because of your huge, loyal love, just like you’ve been forgiving them this whole time since they left Egypt.”

God said, “I forgive them, because you asked. But as surely as I live and as the Glory of God fills the whole Earth—not a single person who saw my Glory and the miracles I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and who has tested me over and over again, ignoring me every time—not one of them will see the land I solemnly promised their ancestors. No one who has treated me with such constant disrespect will see it.
“But my servant Caleb—he’s a different story. He has a different attitude; he follows me with his whole heart. I’ll bring him into the land he scouted, and his kids will inherit it.
“Since the Amalekites and Canaanites are living in the valleys, for now, you need to turn around and go back into the wilderness, following the path to the Red Sea.”

God spoke to Moses and Aaron: “How much longer do I have to put up with all this complaining from this evil community? I have heard the complaints of these grumbling Israelites. Tell them, ‘As I live—this is God’s decree—I’m going to do this to you: Your dead bodies are going to be scattered all over this wilderness—every single one of you twenty years or older who was counted, this whole generation of complainers. Not one of you will enter the land and live there, the land I solemnly promised you, except for Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.’

“Your kids, the ones you said would be captured, I’ll bring them in to enjoy the land you rejected. Meanwhile, your bodies will be rotting in this wilderness. Your children will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, dealing with the consequences of your unfaithfulness, until the last one of your generation is a corpse in the wilderness. You scouted the land for forty days; so your punishment will be a year for each day—a forty-year sentence for your sins. That’ll be a long lesson in what it means to make me unhappy.
“I, God, have spoken. I will definitely do all these things to this entire evil community that has ganged up against me. They will meet their end in this wilderness. They will die here.”

And that’s what happened. The men Moses had sent to scout the land, who came back and spread a bad report about the land, making the whole community grumble against Moses—those men died of a plague before God. Only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh survived out of the men who went to scout the land.

When Moses told all this to the Israelites, they were devastated and mourned for a long time. But early the next morning, they started heading for the high hill country, saying, “We’re here, we’re ready! Let’s go up and take the land God promised us. We sinned, but we’re ready now.”

But Moses said, “Why are you disobeying God’s command again? This isn’t going to work. Don’t attack. God isn’t with you on this—you’ll get totally wrecked by your enemies. The Amalekites and Canaanites are waiting for you, and they’ll kill you. Because you stopped following God obediently, God is not going to be with you in this.”

But they went anyway and climbed up to the high hill country. But the Ark of the Covenant and Moses didn’t move from the camp. The Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in the hills came down, attacked them, and defeated them, chasing them all the way to Hormah.

title: Offerings, Sabbath, and Tassels
paragraphs: God spoke to Moses: "Speak to the Israelites. Tell them, When you enter the land I am giving you and you make a fire-gift sacrifice to God—a burnt offering or a sacrifice for a vow or a freewill offering from your herd or flock—make it a pleasing aroma for God. The one bringing the offering has to present a grain offering of two quarts of fine flour mixed with a quart of oil. With every lamb for the burnt offering or other sacrifice, you gotta prepare a quart of oil and a quart of wine as a drink offering.
For a ram, bring a grain offering of four quarts of fine flour mixed with one and a quarter quarts of oil and the same amount of wine for a drink offering. Present it as a pleasing aroma to God.

When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice for a special vow or a peace offering to God, bring with the bull a grain offering of six quarts of fine flour and two quarts of oil. Also, bring two quarts of wine as a drink offering. It'll be a fire-gift, a pleasing aroma to God.
Every bull or ram, every lamb or young goat, has to be prepped this way. Do this for each one, no matter how many you prepare.

Every native-born Israelite has to follow this procedure when he brings a fire-gift as a pleasing aroma to God. And for future generations, when a foreigner or a visitor living with you for a while presents a fire-gift as a pleasing aroma to God, they have to follow the exact same procedures. The community has the same rules for you and the foreigner living among you. This is the standard rule for all time. You and the foreigner are the same before God. The same laws and regulations apply to both you and the foreigner who lives with you.

God spoke to Moses again: "Tell the People of Israel, when you enter the land I'm bringing you to, and you eat the food from that country, set some aside as an offering for God. From the first batch of your bread dough, make a round loaf as an offering—it's an offering from the threshing floor. For all future generations, you have to make this offering to God from the first batch of dough.

But what if you mess up and don't keep all the commands God gave Moses? Any of the things God commanded you through Moses, from the very first command up until now, and if it was a genuine mistake that the whole community wasn't aware of, then the whole congregation has to sacrifice one young bull as a burnt offering. It's a pleasing aroma to God, and it needs its grain and drink offerings like the rules say, plus a male goat as a sin offering. The priest will make things right for the whole community of Israel, and they'll be forgiven. The sin wasn't on purpose, and they brought the fire-gift and sin offering to God for their mistake. The whole community of Israel, including the foreigners living there, will be forgiven, because everyone was involved in the error.

But if it's just one person who sins by mistake, not realizing what they're doing, they have to bring a one-year-old female goat as a sin offering. The priest will then make things right for the person who accidentally sinned, to make atonement before God so it won't be held against them.
The same rule applies to everyone who sins by mistake; native-born Israelites and foreigners follow the same rules.

But the person, whether native or foreigner, who sins defiantly, blaspheming God, must be cut off from their people. They've despised God's word and violated God's command. That person must be cut off from the community and bear the guilt.

One time, during those years in the wilderness, a man was caught gathering wood on the Sabbath. The people who caught him dragged him in front of Moses, Aaron, and the whole community. They put him in custody until it was clear what should be done with him. Then God told Moses: "The man must be put to death. The whole community has to stone him to death outside the camp."
So the whole community took him outside the camp and stoned him. It was an execution commanded by God through Moses.

God spoke to Moses: "Tell the People of Israel that from now on, they have to make tassels on the corners of their clothes and put a blue thread on each corner tassel. When you look at these tassels, you'll remember and keep all of God's commandments, and you won't get distracted by everything you feel or see that tempts you to be unfaithful. The tassels will be a reminder to remember and obey all my commandments, to live a holy life for God. I am your God who rescued you from Egypt to be your personal God. Yes, I am God, your God."
